- Live AI is **on by default**, and on again after every reload (Owner's choice, Oct 2026). Nothing is sent until an admin with a key presses Send; an admin can switch it off for the current page load.
- Limits: 9 calls and one task per page load, 120 tokens per reply by default (150 at most). **Stop** cancels calls in progress.

## Security: what it does and does not do
- **Live AI is on by default** (Owner, Oct 2026: "always use real ai by default"). The page makes no provider call until an admin with a key presses Send. It never uses web search. Any scripted lines or sample sources must be labeled as such and must never be presented as live research.

About 52,000 points fill the volume, shaped from the traced outline (`mri/brain-outline.json`, shared with `app/src/data/outline.ts`). The brain is a solid white o
- **Access (Owner, Oct 2026):** the page needs a login. Accounts are for adults (18+) only; only admins create accounts. Only admins can send tasks, add, correct or delete memory, change Live AI settings, back up, restore or erase, and manage accounts. Viewers can read memory and watch the live chat
- A live task starts only when an admin has enabled Live AI and presses Send. Brain's memory-maintenance run does not send prompts. Nothing on the page may be scripted or sample data.

## Live AI rules (Owner chose to build it on 2026-10-21; on by default since Oct 2026)

- **On by default and on again after every reload** (Owner, Oct 2026). An admin may switch it off for one page load. Nothing ever sends a task by itself: every live task needs an admin to press Send, and the call caps stay.

Keys live in the browser tab (or the device, only if Owner ticks "remember"). If a key ever appears anywhere in the repo, sto
- **One provider, one key:** the selected API provider/model powers all nine distinct role prompts. This is not a connection to separate apps such as Cursor, Muse, or Xcode; the Perplexity role does not browse or call Perplexity's service.

content.text:
All six requests are built and committed on `brain-app`: real AI only, a guide for adding API keys, small boxes for all text, a glow on the side-panel panes, smoother handoff colours, and a separate colour for each bot. The 78 tests pass and the build's security policy check passes. I haven't seen the page in a real browser, because none runs in this sandbox, so please open `index.html` yourself to judge the look.

## Real AI only
- **No off switch.** Settings can no longer turn real AI off. Nothing is sent until an admin presses Send, and the call limits are unchanged.
- **Key guide.** Until a key is added, the Live chat and Admin tabs show a "Connect real AI" box. It has:
  - steps for each provider and a button that opens that provider's own key page;
  - a box to paste the key, with **Save and test**;
  - a warning if the key looks like it belongs to a different provider;
  - four short tips: where the key is kept, who it is sent to, setting a spend limit, and never pasting it into chat.
  - Viewers instead see that an admin must connect a key.
- **Example tasks.** Example tasks sit above the task box. Clicking one only fills the box; nothing is sent.
- **Default models were out of date, so I changed three of them:**
  - **Google:** Gemini 2.0 Flash‑Lite shut down on June 1, 2026; Google suggests a newer model like gemini-3.1-flash-lite.
  - **xAI:** grok-3, grok-4-0709 and several other old model names were retired on May 15, 2026, and now silently redirect to Grok 4.3.
  - **Anthropic:** now uses `claude-haiku-4-5`.
  - **OpenAI:** stays on `gpt-4o-mini`.
  - A saved setting that names a retired model switches to the new default.
  - **Press Test once per provider.** The newer Gemini and Grok models may spend part of the 120-token reply limit on thinking, and I can't call them from here to check.

## Boxes and glow
- **Small boxes everywhere.** The login, header, labels in the 3D view, chat, memory and admin settings all use small bordered boxes.
- **Login.** The login now has three small fact tiles under the form.
- **Side-panel glow.** Only the panes in the side panel (or under it, on narrow screens) get the glow. They are dark glass with a faint blue-purple-rose line on the left and right edges. The 3D view and the login card don't have it.
- I didn't open cloudflare.com; the box style follows its general look of small bordered tiles.

## Bot colours
Memory dots keep their blue, green and orange type colours, as you chose. Each bot's own colour is used for:
- its dot in the brain;
- its node in the Team view;
- the glow on its chat messages;
- its coverage chip;
- its handoffs.

![Each bot's colour, with the memory type colours and the failed red for comparison]({{artifact:18c92251-8021-4d65-8ba9-d413e99123b9}})

The closest pair is Claude's clay and the red used when a bot fails. A failed bot also gets a ✕ mark on its chip, but I can shift Claude's colour if they look too alike.

## Passing data between bots
What I changed so the handoffs look smoother and only show data that really moved:
1. **Colour.** The light changes smoothly from the sender's colour to the receiver's, and bot dots fade between colours instead of jumping.
2. **Motion.** The light speeds up gently and slows down as it arrives. It leaves a fading trail, and the path keeps glowing for 1.4 seconds afterwards.
3. **Size label.** Each handoff carries a small box showing how many words were really passed.
4. **Memory context.** Saved memories sent with a task fly from their dot to the first bot.
5. **Grok Bot.** Grok Bot reads every earlier handoff, so each finished bot now sends a light to it.

![Handoff from Gemini to Muse over time; "84 words" is only an example]({{artifact:30a7c2be-64fb-4039-8a70-4514210cda9f}})

Ideas for later, not built yet:
- **Streaming replies.** Light would flow while words are actually arriving, which would look the most real.
- **Faster bots move faster.** Speed would be based on each bot's real response time.
- **Task summary.** A chart at the end of a task would show how much passed between each pair of bots.
- **Brightness from history.** Paths that carry more over many sessions would glow brighter.

The two commits are `c2fabed` (real AI, boxes, glow, handoffs) and `7c65a63` (bot colours). They aren't merged or pushed.

Files are in the tray:
- `handoff_colour_preview.png` — the handoff colour timeline
- `bot_colours.png` — the bot colour chart

content.text:
I built all four ideas from my last message, plus the Tasks list from the mockup. They are in commit `5ce620e` on `brain-app`. The 89 tests pass and the rebuilt `index.html` passes the security policy check. It isn't merged or pushed, and I haven't tried it in a real browser or against the real providers.

The 5-task picture I sent earlier is only an image. Brain's no-scripted-data rule means I didn't put example tasks into the app, so the list fills only from tasks you really run.

**What's new in the side panel and the brain:**
1. **Streaming replies.** Each bot's text now appears in the chat as it arrives, with a "streaming · N words" tag. In the brain, that bot's dot flashes each time a new piece of text comes in. Viewer tabs on the same computer see the text grow too. If a provider sends the whole reply at once instead, Brain reads it the old way.
2. **Tasks list.** It shows the running task and your saved tasks, newest first, five at a time.
   - Each task box has its nine bot dots in their own colours: filled means covered, ringed means working, red means failed, and dashed means skipped.
   - A status pill shows "Running", "8 of 8", "7 of 8 · 1 failed" or "Stopped", with one line of detail (for a failed bot, its real error message).
   - Clicking a task opens it. This replaces the old "Show saved sessions" link.
3. **Flow box.** After a task, a small box shows how many words really passed between each pair of bots, as bars in the two bots' colours. It also shows how long each bot took to reply. This is saved with the task.
4. **Speed from reply time.** A handoff light travels faster when the sender answered quickly and slower when it took long. It is never faster than 0.9 s or slower than 4.2 s.
5. **Glow from history.** Paths that carried more words across all your saved tasks glow a little brighter in the brain.

**Two things to know:**
- **Five tasks needs five reloads.** The limit of one task per page load is unchanged, because the project rules say not to raise limits. Say if you want it changed.
- **Try one task per provider.** The streaming code is tested only against fake replies here. If streaming fails with a provider, the task chat will show the real error rather than make something up.

The only new file is the mockup, [side_panel_5_tasks_mockup.png]({{artifact:7f0b39e1-5bfe-4679-96d7-affd6e79bfcf}}); the app changes are in the repo. To merge once you're happy with it: `git checkout main && git merge --ff-only brain-app`.

        if x1<x0 or y1<y0: continue

Everything you asked for is built and committed on a new branch, `improve`, in 8 commits. The 85 tests pass and the built `index.html` passes its security policy check. Nothing is merged or pushed yet.

**Only AI makes results.** Memory is now written by the team, not by Brain on its own.
- **Grok Bot files memory.** After each task, Grok Bot makes one more real AI call and saves up to 3 memories. If it names something already saved, that memory gets stronger instead of copied. The next task gets matching memories as context, so the team learns from itself. That setting is now on by default; you can turn it off in the Admin tab.
- **iOS tasks save nothing new.** The memory call counts toward the 9-call limit. An iOS task already uses all 9 calls, so it gets a status note instead of a memory.
- **The old local learner is gone.** I removed the text-analysis learner and the "Run Brain now" button. Memories it made earlier are archived: kept in your encrypted storage, but never shown or sent.
- **Your own notes stay.**
- **The chat shows only AI replies.** Brain's own notes now go to the status line. Error reasons go on the bot's chip and the Tasks list.

**Minecraft font only.** It's "Minecraft" by Craftron Gaming, which DaFont lists as 100% Free, and it's built into the page.
- **Sizes:** body text is 16px and titles are 32px. Those are the only sizes where its pixels stay sharp; other sizes blur, as the preview shows.
- **No bold:** the font has one weight, so faked bold is turned off.
- **Wider panel:** the side panel went from 430px to 520px to fit the wider letters.
- **Missing symbols:** the font only covers basic letters, numbers and punctuation. Symbols like ✓ ✕ · → … still show in the system font.

![The Minecraft font at the chosen sizes, shown at 2× zoom]({{artifact:d472364f-42f8-4adf-aa88-d4e50e0d2bd0}})

**Front-view streaks fixed.** Two changes work together:
- only the surface nearest the camera glows now, so folds behind it no longer show through;
- the glowing shell no longer has the small fold ripples. The faint fold lines are still drawn.

The side outline is unchanged.

![Brain outline: now, nearest surface only, and nearest surface plus smooth shell (the change built)]({{artifact:73b43d12-50ac-4f55-b7b5-d48f20b6c72d}})

**Clean-up.**
- **CLAUDE.md** now says to edit `app/src` and rebuild.
- **`legacy/`** is removed.
- **Formatting and lint checks** come from Biome. I used it instead of ESLint because ESLint's TypeScript plugin doesn't support TypeScript 7. Reformatting didn't change the built page beyond spacing.
- **The task steps** moved out of `store.ts` into `lib/run-task.ts`.
- **GitHub now runs all checks** on every push, including a new Playwright test in real Chromium. That test has never run, because no browser works in this sandbox. Its first run will be on GitHub or on your Mac (`npm run e2e:install`, then `npm run e2e`).
- **Stray cache folder trashed.** I had created an npm download cache at `~/Brain/npmcache-tmp` by mistake and moved it to your Trash.

cd ~/Brain/Brain && git checkout main && git merge --ff-only improve && git push

Run one API operation found with search. params is a flat object holding the operation's path, query and body parameters as described by its inputSchema.

Schema:

### multi-execute

Run up to 20 API operations in order, stopping at the first failure. A params value that is exactly "$steps.<i>.<path>" is replaced by that value from the result of earlier step <i> (dot-separated keys; numbers index arrays), e.g. "$steps.0.0.id".

### dns_records_save

Add custom DNS resource records or update TTL. Records are matched using case-insensitive comparison, except for TXT records; a value this brand rewrites when storing it (a trailing dot on host-like values, quoting on a CAA value) matches either as submitted or as read back; an SRV record is matched on its service, protocol, priority, weight, port and target, and its name is ignored. MX records are checked against the domain Mail Settings before anything is written: when Mail Settings are not Custom MX (for example Email Forwarding, Private Email, Gmail or No Email Service) Namecheap drops MX records, so the call is refused with a message naming the mode and saying to switch Mail Settings to Custom MX in the Namecheap dashboard (Advanced DNS), and nothing is saved; with `force` set, the other records are written and each MX record is listed in `failed` with the Mail Settings reason. After writing, the zone is re-read to confirm the records persisted: a record accepted and then dropped by another DNS feature on the domain is reported as a conflict instead of being counted as saved; with `force` set, such records are listed in `failed` with a reason and `saved` counts only the records that persisted. If the call fails with infrastructure.serviceUnavailable, or reports a record as not saved because a connected service could not complete the request, the records may still have been saved: read them with dns_records_get before saving again. Requires the dnsrecords:write scope.

### domain_purchase_link

Start buying a domain for the customer through Namecheap's own consent and payment page — not this chat. The customer chooses their own payment method there. Never offer this link to recover from a purchase attempt whose outcome is unknown or that may already have billed: call `domains_list` first and offer it only if the domain is genuinely not registered, or the customer risks paying twice. Returns a `consentUrl` the customer must open themselves; nothing is charged by this call. The customer approves and pays entirely on namecheap.com, and the page then shows them the result of the purchase; there is no follow-up step for the agent or the customer. Do not report the domain as bought on the strength of this call: confirm with `domains_list` before telling the customer it is theirs. Set `autoRenew` to choose whether the domain and its WHOIS privacy renew automatically, charging the customer again each term; it defaults to on when omitted, and the consent page shows the choice to the customer without letting them change it there (they can change it afterwards in their account). Term length and contacts cannot be set through this tool — the consent page has no field for them. If the domain turns out to be unavailable, status is "unavailable" rather than an error. Requires the domains:billing scope.

### domain_set_nameservers

Change a domain's registrar-level nameservers. Set `provider` to "basic" to switch the domain to this brand's default nameservers (omit `hosts`), or to "custom" to point it at your own 2–12 `hosts`. Re-applying the state a domain is already in (e.g. setting "basic" when it is already basic) is not an error: the domain is read first, nothing is written, and the answer is the current `{ provider, hosts }` with the note "Already set; nothing changed.". Check domain availability. Accepts 1–20 domain names, checked in groups of up to 5. A domain whose check timed out comes back with `result: checkTimedOut` and is neither available nor taken; check those names again later. Each available domain includes the USD `price` that would be charged to register it (standard and premium alike); when a price cannot be determined it carries `priceUnavailableReason` instead. For a standard domain the price covers the shortest term the TLD allows, reported as `price.pricedYears` — for a TLD with a multi-year minimum (e.g. 2 years) `price.amount` is the whole-term total, not a yearly figure. `price.pricePerYear` is that total divided by the term, so a yearly figure is always available; a premium price reports neither field. `minRegisterPeriodInYears` and `maxRegisterPeriodInYears` report the term that TLD permits; both are omitted when the range cannot be determined.
